1) Bug scenario and root cause  
   The user is using the Bash ANSI-C quoting form:
     echo $'foo\nbar'  
   but Prism’s Bash grammar only recognizes ordinary single‐ or double‐quoted strings (and here-docs). It never treats `$'…'` as a string container, so the interior escapes (e.g. `\n`) are never highlighted as entities. We need to inject a new string‐mode before the “normal string” rule, one that matches `$'…'` with the existing escape‐sequence subgrammar.

The existing “normal”-string rule only sees bare '…' or "…", so anything starting with $'…' just falls through to the general punctuation/escape patterns (and the “\n” sequences end up tricking the engine).

The fix is to insert an extra string-pattern into the Prism.languages.bash “string” array, *before* the normal-string rule, that will match $'…' (ANSI-C quoting) and apply the same insideString sub-grammar.
